name: Drypoint
summary: A steel or diamond needle scratches the plate and pushes up a burr of metal along each furrow. The burr holds ink and prints as a soft velvety black line that wears down after a few dozen impressions.

philosophy.core_thesis: A needle that scratches bare copper throws up a burr. The burr prints as a soft black line that no acid and no burin can make.
design_principles: Draw straight on the bare plate with a hard needle; no ground and no acid.
Keep the burr: do not scrape it off, because it holds the ink and makes the velvet edge.
Draw the darkest areas with dense, near-parallel lines, and keep the light areas open.
Wipe the plate with a thin film of ink left in the field, for a plate tone.
Expect the line to thin after 20–50 impressions, and number the edition on that count.
Combine with etching only when a firm line is also needed; keep the burr lines for the shadows.
anti_patterns: A clean, hard line of even width
Halftone dots or a smooth gradient
A long edition with no loss of the burr

process.matrix: Copper or zinc plate, no acid
process.image_making: Needle scratched directly; burr kept on the plate
process.edition: 20-50 good impressions before the burr flattens

inks.strategy: One intaglio ink, black or brown-black, wiped by hand with a film of tone left in the field.

screening.rule: Make the tone with open lines, 20–40 lines an inch, that thicken into velvet black where the burr is rich.

registration.rule: One plate prints the whole image; a colour print needs a plate for each ink.

substrate.stock: Dampened laid or Japan paper, warm cream.
substrate.finish: Soft and absorbent, with a surface that takes the burr.

surface.impression: A plate mark of 3–6 mm; the inked burr stands as a raised, velvet line on the sheet.
surface.sheen: Matt and velvety in the lines; the plate tone gives a slight sheen.
surface.texture: Blurred line edges, and a soft tone round the line where the burr held the ink.

marks: velvety burr line with blurred edge
furrow lines that thin over an edition

positive: biblical crowd scene in deep burr shadow

evidence.title: Christ Crucified Between the Two Thieves (The Three Crosses)

emotion.target_response: Intimate, quiet intensity: the viewer sees a drawing that was scratched, with a warm and deep black.

use_cases: stationery and invitations with a hand-made look
avoid_when: The design needs a large edition with exact repeats.
The line must stay hard and even.

modifiers.how: Etch the line in acid, so that it holds for a long edition; keep a few burr lines for the dark areas.
Add a rosin grain under the line and bite it in steps.
